  (a) make the promise true — return the slot's model UNQUALIFIED when no class is configured and
      the slot is at its built-in default. Preserves byte-identity; costs a special case.
  (b) accept the qualified form and CORRECT the plan's byte-identical claim, updating the existing
      test. Arguably better long-term (a qualified id is unambiguous and is what provenance wants),
      but it is a real behaviour change that must be stated, not slipped in.
Recommend (b) with the claim corrected, but this is a plan-level decision — it changes what 172e
promises, so it should be re-reviewed rather than chosen by the implementer.

SEPARATELY, a legitimate contract change still pending:
test_verifier_cfg_honors_explicit_operator_override pins the OLD rule ("an operator who explicitly
chose a non-default model keeps it"). That rule IS the defect 172e removes — under classes the
verifier always resolves `standard` and the operator steers it via the class config. That test must
be updated to the new contract WITH justification in the commit message. It is not a test to
"fix away" quietly; it encodes the behaviour this ticket intentionally changes.

must be synced to eb58 comment 4.

1. A FOURTH LADDER SITE. workflow/runners.py:120, DefaultBatchRunner.run(), does

compiled_state.description:
# Verifier paths resolve the standard class

## Context / Problem
Three separate code paths pick the verifier model, and all three break off the default provider:
- `review_kernel/verify.py:269` — `verifier_default if model == default_model else (model or
  verifier_default)`. Any non-default model (every Bedrock id) reads as an explicit operator choice,
  so the downgrade silently stops applying.
- `completion.py:332` — `if cfg.model == DEFAULT_MODEL: cfg = replace(cfg, model=...)`. Same inversion,
  separate path.
- `workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — declares no `model:` on any step, so all four code-review passes
  take `cfg.model` and it never downgrades at all. Its Pass-2 pins `temperature: 0` for greedy
  verification, so running it on the frontier model also loses determinism.

## Approach
Replace all three with a single resolution of the `standard` class. The equality test DISAPPEARS
rather than being repaired: "the operator chose a verifier" is now expressed by configuring the
`standard` slot, not by comparing `cfg.model` to a constant. One mechanism fixes three gates.

**Alternative rejected — fixing the equality rule in place.** It would need a new way to distinguish
"operator override" from "provider change" when both arrive as `cfg.model`, and it would have to be
repeated on all three paths.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` — add `resolve_model_string(value)`: the ONE place that knows the
  reserved class vocabulary. Returns the resolved id for `trivial`/`standard`/`frontier`, and any
  other string UNCHANGED.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — `resolve_model` calls it via a LAZY, function-level import. A
  module-level import is IMPOSSIBLE here: `model_classes` imports from `config`, and its docstring
  forbids the reverse. Function-level is the established pattern in this file already
  (`config.py:108`, `:566`, `:768`).
- `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py` — `resolve_verifier_model`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` — `_verifier_cfg` (line 46). A consumer the plan had NOT
  enumerated, with two further call sites at `xcheck.py:198` and `xcheck.py:336`.
- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` — the parallel equality test at line 332.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — express the per-pass class as `model: standard`.
- `tests/unit/` — per-path resolution tests.

NOT in scope, and deliberately: the ladder path
(`production_batch_runner.py:93`, `code_review/batch_runner.py:55`) is sibling task 7761. Both
tickets call the SAME `resolve_model_string`, which is why the vocabulary lives in one function.

## Testing
Contract tier: the observable is which model id each pass resolves to under a given class config.
- each of the FOUR verifier paths resolves the `standard` class: `resolve_verifier_model`,
  `_verifier_cfg`, `completion.py`'s equality test, and code-review.yaml's verify step.
- with classes configured for a non-default provider, none of them falls back to the framework
  default (the regression this ticket exists for).
- code review's Pass-2 resolves `standard`, not `frontier`.
- a literal model id passed to `resolve_model_string` comes back UNCHANGED (the back-compat
  guarantee that keeps every existing workflow YAML working).

## MECHANISM (decided on parent eb58 — corrected; do not re-derive)

**A workflow step names a class by using the class name as its `model:` value.** The three class
names are RESERVED VALUES in the EXISTING model-string space — no new `class:` key, no schema
change. In YAML: `model: standard`.

**There is NO single interception point.** An earlier version of this plan claimed
`config.resolve_model` was "the ONE funnel every step model passes through". That was wrong three
ways, all verified in source:

1. `config.py` cannot import `model_classes` at module level — the dependency runs the other way and
   `model_classes`'s own docstring forbids the reverse.
2. `model_ladder` never reaches `resolve_model`: `production_batch_runner.py:93` does
   `dataclasses.replace(cfg, model=req.model_ladder[0])`.
3. The verifier paths never reach it either — `resolve_verifier_model` is its own path, as is
   `_verifier_cfg`.

So the shape is ONE FUNCTION, several CALL SITES:

    model_classes.resolve_model_string(value: str) -> str
        "trivial" | "standard" | "frontier"  ->  resolve via load_class_slots()
        anything else                        ->  return unchanged

This ticket wires the VERIFIER call sites; sibling 7761 wires the LADDER ones. Keeping the
vocabulary in one function is what stops those two tickets from drifting apart.

REJECTED — a new `class:` key: forks a step schema `runs.py` documents as closed, and makes
`model: standard` vs `class: standard` a silent ambiguity.

REJECTED — resolving at YAML load time: the mapping depends on process-scoped env/CLI layers, so it
would freeze the wrong value in a long-lived process and be invisible to `provider_provenance`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts plan-review Pass-2/Pass-4 resolve the `standard` class
- [ ] a test asserts the completion verifier resolves the `standard` class
- [ ] a test asserts code-review's verify step resolves the `standard` class rather than `cfg.model`
- [ ] a test asserts that with classes configured for a non-default provider, no verifier path resolves
      a model belonging to a different provider
- [ ] `grep -rn "== DEFAULT_MODEL" src/rebar/llm/` returns no verifier-selection site

- [ ] a test asserts a workflow step whose `model:` is the literal string `standard` resolves to the
      configured standard class's model id, and that a step whose `model:` is a literal model id
      resolves to that id UNCHANGED (the byte-for-byte back-compat guarantee)
- [ ] a test asserts the Pass-2/Pass-4 verifier resolves the `standard` class REGARDLESS of what
      `cfg.model` is — including when `cfg.model` is a Bedrock id. MEASURED today:
      `resolve_verifier_model` downgrades ONLY on an exact match against the bare `claude-opus-4-8`,
      so even `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` (the SAME model, merely provider-qualified) silently keeps
      Pass-2 on opus. This criterion fails against the current implementation, so it cannot pass
      vacuously
- [ ] a test enumerates the consumers of `resolve_verifier_model` and asserts each resolves the
